literal: Guard against faults indeed as a matter of importance; fault indeed is the enemy that brings ruin.
translation: Guard against faults as a matter of utmost importance; for one's own fault is the very enemy that brings ultimate ruin.
modern: குற்றங்களை ஒரு முக்கியமான கடமையாகக் கருதி அவற்றிலிருந்து தம்மைக் காத்துக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்; ஏனெனில், குற்றமே ஒருவருக்கு அழிவைத் தரும் பகையாகும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the critical need to avoid personal faults and flaws. The author advises that guarding oneself against committing faults (kuṟṟam) should be treated as a matter of supreme importance (poruḷ). This is because a person's own flaws are not minor errors, but rather the very enemy (pakai) that brings about their ultimate ruin (aṟṟam). By personifying faults as a destructive enemy, the verse warns that self-destruction comes from within through one's own uncorrected mistakes.
